description: Second reference table — Klatt 1980 + Mullen 2006 vowel formants for /a/, /e/, /o/, /u/. Captured from NotebookLM Q&A 2026-05-28 against the cited primary sources. Complements tables/vowel_formants.json (Peterson-Barney 1952) — use whichever calibration the ear says is right. Do NOT auto-replace VOWELS in forge/src/main.rs without explicit go-ahead; the existing 'FROZEN' comment there is load-bearing.

sources.klatt_1980: Dennis H. Klatt, 'Software for a cascade/parallel formant synthesizer', JASA 67(3):971-995, 1980. Klatt holds F4 (and F5) constant at 3300 Hz across vowels — 'higher-frequency resonators do not vary as much and could be held constant with little decrement in output sound quality.'
sources.mullen_2006: Jack Mullen, 'Physical modelling of the vocal tract with the 2D digital waveguide mesh', PhD thesis, University of York, 2006. Per-vowel F4 values; adult-male averages.
sources.peterson_barney_1952: See tables/vowel_formants.json — the current code base uses this. Adult-male averages. F4 not provided in that table.

note_on_F4: Klatt held F4=3300 constant. Mullen measured per-vowel F4. The Forge's VOWELS constant is F1/F2/F3 only; if F4 is wired in later, prefer Klatt's 3300 constant unless the ear says otherwise.
phonetic_mapping_notes: English vowel labels are slippery. The Forge's 'Ee' is the high front /i/ (as in 'see'), NOT /e/ (as in 'bed'). The 'Oo' is /u/ (as in 'boot'), NOT /o/ (as in 'bought'). When wiring this table into UI overlays, surface the IPA + example word, not just an English-sound nickname.
